prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study describes a 54-year-old woman with multiple autoimmune conditions who experienced continuous jerking in three fingers of her right hand.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: A brain scan taken during the seizures showed increased blood flow in the part of the left brain that controls the right hand.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Monitoring of brain and muscle activity showed electrical signals in the left brain appearing just before the muscle twitches in the right little finger.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The patient's symptoms improved with steroid treatment, but the medication had to be stopped because it caused a serious worsening of her blood sugar levels.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Other treatments, including different forms of steroids, immune therapy, and several anti-seizure drugs, did not work for her condition.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Treatment with the drug Rituximab resulted in a complete and lasting stop of the seizures, which was still present 18 months later.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The case suggests that this specific type of continuous seizure can be a sign of widespread autoimmune disease even when there is no inflammation of the brain.
facts.subject: humans
